subject: SLO reproducibility ops checklist and prompt curation
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Rivera <jordan.rivera@novaretail.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@novaretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLO reproducibility ops checklist and prompt curation

Hi Jordan / Priya —

Thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed handoff so we can get the benchmark window scheduled:

Goals we heard on the call
- Latency SLOs: 95th percentile end-to-end response (streaming first token) <= 250 ms, p99 tail <= 600 ms for single-stream sessions.
- Throughput target: sustained 400 reqs/min for the checkout flow (peak bursts to 600 reqs/min).
- Concurrency: up to 150 concurrent active sessions during peak.
- Streaming behavior: token-by-token SSE to the browser; clients depend on first-token arrival & steady token throughput.

Immediate asks from our side
1) Please share the prompt pack you want included in the qualification run (canonical prompts + negative cases + explicit edge-case examples). We need variants for: short query (<= 40 tokens), medium (100-200 tokens), and long context (up to 1,200 tokens).
2) Provide a small representative dataset (100 obfuscated records) we can use for local reproducibility. If any PII, please obfuscate.
3) Confirm whether NovaRetail will accept the following measurement definitions:
   - "First-token latency": time from HTTP request accept to first-streamed token bytes on the client.
   - "Stable throughput window": average tokens/sec measured over 30s windows after the 10s warmup.
   - "Tail metric": p99 computed across all requests in the run.

What we'll deliver before the benchmark run
- A run-config.yaml (load profile + seed + warmup rules) and harness-instructions.md describing how to replay locally.
- A checklist (ops-runbook) for concurrency warmup, KV-cache priming, and deterministic RNG seeding to improve reproducibility.

Proposed next steps / timeline
- You share prompt pack + obfuscated sample by EOD Monday 2027-08-16.
- We prepare harness and run-config by Wednesday 2027-08-18.
- Trial run with our dedicated pool Thursday 2027-08-19; full run (customer-observed) week of 2027-08-23 if all good.

Attachments we requested: prompt pack (JSON) and a short csv describing token-length distribution.

Open questions (please confirm):
- Do you require redaction for logs exported to us during the run? (we can mask at ingestion)
- Any session affinity concerns for your client that would change routing assumptions?

Thanks — looping in Ben and Marissa to coordinate the run logistics.

— Soojin

Thanks for the clear recap, Soojin. Confirming a few items from our side and attaching the initial prompt pack.

Clarifications / constraints from NovaRetail
- Our typical request sizes: 55% short (<50 tokens), 35% medium (50–220 tokens), 10% long (>220 tokens, up to 1,200 tokens).
- Concurrency model: clients open a websocket or SSE and maintain one live stream per checkout session; average session length 35s.
- For legal reasons we cannot share raw customer text. Attached is an obfuscated prompt pack (novaretail_prompt_pack_v1.json) and a 100-record synthetic dataset for local runs.
- We'll accept the measurement definitions you proposed; please make the first-token timestamp visible in the measurement artifacts.

Attachments included (zipped package): novaretail_prompt_pack_v1.json, novaretail_synthetic_100.csv

Log redaction: we ask that Redwood redact any full-text payloads before any long-term storage. Short-term access during runs for debugging is fine; we will provide a reviewer.

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO reproducibility ops checklist and prompt curation

Thanks Jordan — received the pack and the synthetic dataset. I reviewed novaretail_prompt_pack_v1.json and sketched the reproducibility steps below.

Key notes for the harness and measurement (summary)
- Deterministic seeding: our harness will apply a fixed RNG seed for prompt sampling. We will include the seed in the run metadata so you can re-run locally and reproduce.
- KV-cache priming: for streaming flows with session affinity, we'll run a 10-minute warmup at 10% load to populate model KV caches for common product contexts.
- Batch sizing and continuous batching: for reproducibility we will run two modes:
  1) "Production-mode" (continuous batching enabled, dynamic batch sizes up to 32 tokens) to measure economic throughput.
  2) "Deterministic-mode" (batch size fixed, disabled micro-batching) to capture lowest possible variance for tail metrics.
- Measurement definitions (as we plan to emit):
  - first_token_latency_ms (ISO8601 timestamp + ms)
  - total_tokens_generated
  - tokens_per_second_windowed (30s windows)
  - p50/p95/p99 over both first_token_latency_ms and tokens_per_second_windowed

Run-config highlights (attached run-config.yaml)
- seed: 1729
- warmup: 600s at 10% of target concurrency
- steady_state: 1800s at 100% target load
- collectors: prometheus + checkpointed artifact of raw event stream (masked)

Repro checklist we will drop into harness-instructions.md
- exact command-lines to run the harness locally
- how to replay the 100 synthetic records deterministically
- how to switch between production/deterministic modes
- where to find the log artifacts (masked) and the p99 report

Proposed deliverables by Thu 2027-08-19 EOD
- run-config.yaml (attached)
- harness-instructions.md (attached)
- initial trial run summary and raw artifact bundle (masked) by 2027-08-20

Open question: for the deterministic-mode runs we will disable dynamic fallback to smaller models. Is NovaRetail comfortable that deterministic runs may not reflect your production fallback behavior? If not, we can run both modes and annotate differences.

Action items
- Jordan to confirm redaction acceptance and observational window (you said 2027-08-24 AM PT).
- Ben / Marissa to confirm which Redwoods pool we allocate for the customer-observed run (Ben, can you confirm availability?).

Thanks — attaching the run configs now.

— Soojin
